intro.text: Mountains on the eastern side of Jah Keved, home of the Unkalaki, called Horneaters by outsiders.

description.text: The air on the peaks is noticeably thin; Rock calls other Rosharans "airsick lowlanders". The peaks block clouds, so the land to their west gets little rain except from highstorms.

Each peak's summit has collapsed into a crater filled with a lake of warm water, which the Unkalaki call an Ocean. The heat creates a pocket of livable land, often warmer than the lowlands, where grass and fruit trees grow.
Unkalaki villages sit on the peaks, and the Jokasha Monastery on the western slopes. The single spanreed station may be more than a week's travel from a village.
Chulls breed on the southern slopes. The Horneaters eat every part of chulls and other animals, horns and shells included, which gave them their name.

items.text: Unkalaki legend says they became outcasts for their fighting prowess and asked the gods to make them a new home.
Over time the Unkalaki rejoined Rosharan society, and by the end of the Era of Solitude Horneaters were common in the great cities of Jah Keved and Alethkar.
Though the Unkalaki live within Jah Keved's borders, they are treated much like a sovereign nation; different peaks occasionally fight one another.
After the Battle of Narak, Rock's family came to find him with news that something was very wrong in their homeland.
